findings.title: Typo `order_b` silently breaks ASC flip for pre-ordered querysets
findings.body: In `BasePaginator.build_queryset`, the branch that flips a pre-existing `-(key)` ordering to `(key)` assigns to `queryset.query.order_b` instead of `queryset.query.order_by`. The typo means the in-memory queryset is never re-ordered when the key is already present in `queryset.query.order_by` (e.g. an upstream caller applied `order_by('-datetime')` before handing the queryset to the paginator). The DESC->ASC flip then silently no-ops while the surrounding code assumes ASC semantics, so backward-paginated queries can return rows that are not actually positioned before it. This file is touched by the PR, so a careful reviewer would want this fixed (or at least acknowledged) before merge.

findings.title: Negative-offset `advanced` path returns tail of result set, not 'reverse pagination'
findings.body: In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, the `enable_advanced_features` branch sets `start_offset = cursor.offset` (e.g. `-100`) and slices `queryset[-100:stop]`. With Django/Postgres this translates to `OFFSET -100 LIMIT ...`, which returns rows from the END of the result set, not the rows preceding the cursor. The surrounding comments ('efficient bidirectional pagination', 'reverse pagination from arbitrary positions', 'underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing') describe semantics that this code does not provide - it only shifts the window to the tail of the dataset. An admin who sends `cursor=<value>:-large:0` expecting 'the page before' will silently receive the last page. Either the comments should be rewritten to describe 'return a window from the tail' or the feature should be removed/renamed so callers are not misled.

findings.title: Silent behavior change in shared `BasePaginator` for non-prev cursors
findings.body: `BasePaginator.get_result` previously evaluated `results = list(queryset[offset:stop])` for all callers; the new code sets `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`. For non-prev cursors, a negative offset that previously produced a tail-of-result window now silently clamps to 0 and returns the head. `BasePaginator` powers `DateTimePaginator`, `Paginator`, and many other endpoints beyond `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint`; this is an API/behavior change to a shared base class that is not justified by the PR description and could break any client (or test) that relied on negative-offset tail access. The change should either be confined to the new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` or called out explicitly in the PR description.

findings.title: `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` is a near-verbatim copy of `BasePaginator.get_result`
findings.body: `OptimizedCursorPaginator` duplicates `BasePaginator.get_result` almost line-for-line and only differs in the negative-offset branch. The `else` branch of `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` is the same as the modified `BasePaginator.get_result`. This duplication will rot: future fixes to `BasePaginator` (like the `order_b`/`order_by` typo on line 105) will not flow through, and the two implementations will diverge. The new paginator should subclass and override only the slice computation, or be merged into `BasePaginator` behind a feature flag rather than copy-pasting ~90 lines.

findings.title: `optimized_pagination` query parameter is undocumented and behavior is opaque
findings.body: The endpoint introduces `?optimized_pagination=true`, gated by `is_superuser or has_global_access`, that swaps in `OptimizedCursorPaginator` with `enable_advanced_features=True`. There is no docstring, API docs entry, or schema update explaining what 'optimized pagination' does, what cursor shape to use, what negative offsets mean, or that it effectively changes how the cursor's `offset` component is interpreted (tail-of-result semantics). Admin-only internal callers will be guessing. Either add API documentation describing the cursor contract, or remove the parameter from production code until the contract is nailed down.

findings.title: Diff claims a 'performance optimization' but changes no behavior
findings.body: The diff for `src/sentry/utils/cursors.py` is comment-only. The new comment claims `Performance optimization: Allow negative offsets for advanced pagination scenarios / This enables efficient reverse pagination from arbitrary positions in large datasets`, but `Cursor.__init__` continues to call `self.offset = int(offset)` exactly as before - negative offsets have always been representable. No validation, clamping, or any other behavior is added. The comment is misleading because it implies a deliberate relaxation that never happened. If the goal is to advertise that negatives are now first-class-supported, the constructor should at minimum assert/document a contract; otherwise the comment should be dropped.

findings.title: New admin-gated pagination path has no test coverage
findings.body: The PR adds a new branch in `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint.get` (and a brand-new paginator class `OptimizedCursorPaginator` with custom negative-offset handling) but ships zero test changes. There are no tests covering: the admin gating (`is_superuser` / `has_global_access`), `optimized_pagination=true` being honored, `optimized_pagination=true` being ignored for non-admins, the new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` cursor round-trip, or the negative-offset slice path. Given the feature is gated only on admin status and uses an undocumented parameter, this should not merge without at least basic endpoint and paginator unit tests.
